newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's central bank denies budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's central bank denies budget deficit.

text.p: Disowning a mid-year report widely credited to it, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) on Friday denied that the nation recorded a budget deficit of 6.577 billion naira ($82.68 million) in the first half of 1996.
"The CBN wishes to state categorically that its report on the developments in the economy during the first half of 1996 has not been officially released," it said in a statement.
"Furthermore, the CBN wishes to inform the general public that the report under reference was based on provisional data," it added.

The central bank report released on Wednesday to news media including Reuters announced the deficit which was a sharp contrast to an eight billion naira surplus for the same period announced last month by finance minister Anthony Ani.
The bank, however, explained in the report that the difference between the deficit and the surplus reported by Ani was due to conflicting figures for debt servicing.

"While the federal ministry of finance recorded 22 billion naira and six billion naira for external and domestic debt service payments, actual payments in the central bank indicated 26.804 billion naira and 12.133 billion, respectively," it said.

Friday's central bank statement said: "While it is true that in an earlier draft of the report there was reference to a provisional budget deficit, the federal ministry of finance has since August 1996 given the necessary advice to the CBN to use its other accumulated revenue with the bank to fund its account.
"Consequently, the true position is that the federal government recorded a budget surplus of eight billion naira in the first half of 1996," it added.

Official sources said the military government has been embarrassed by the release of the draft report to the press in Lagos and investigations were underway to see why this was done without approval of the central bank higher authorities who are in Abuja.
"The report is capable of causing a credibility crisis for the government," one said.

A key plank of General Sani Abacha's economic policy is to control budget deficits which balloned to 70 billion naira during the administration of former military ruler General Ibrahim Babangida now retired.
The government says it recorded a surplus of one billion naira last year, the first in a long time and promised to do better this year through its tight fiscal policy.
